note: Checkpoint E4 baseline: canonical INTEGER / BINARY / MIXED solving and BRANCH-AND-BOUND are exercised directly against engine/source/plumline-engine.js through the canonical harness (E4 phase). E4 is structural and contractual: NO engine byte, mirror byte, constant, tolerance, branching policy, variable selection, node order, tie-breaking, pruning, limit, default, result, error, status, stopReason or public output changed. The engine SHA stays 5d68ed17...; the mirror SHA stays 6190cb47... Final public status/stopReason/optimalityProven semantics, independent verification, localised messages, Worker and mirror reconciliation remain E5/E6. Current behaviours below are COMPATIBILITY CHARACTERISATIONS, not endorsements.

mirror.status: unchanged since E0; legacy add-on twin; NOT reconciled in E4

exports.note: E4 list is a SEPARATE closed set, not a copy of E2 or E3. The harness serves all phases from one infrastructure; it never merges the export sets. E2 stays 24, E3 stays 22.

constants.INTEGRALITY_TOLERANCE: 1e-6 (isWhole_ literal; NOT a named ENGINE constant)
constants.note: All ENGINE.* constants unchanged. isWhole_ uses a literal 1e-6 tolerance, distinct from EPSILON.

branch_selection_C: solveIntegerProgram_ inner loop: first fractional index in `wanted` order
node_construction_D: solveIntegerProgram_ explore(extra, depth): ceil branch (>= ceil) FIRST, then floor (<= floor)
incumbent_pruning_F: solveIntegerProgram_ best/improves logic; prune by bound, by infeasible dead-end, by integrality
dispatcher_D: optimise_ (L33): integerIndices_ empty -> solveLinearProgram_ (E3); non-empty -> solveIntegerProgram_ (E4)

domain_schema.integer_spec: model.integer: undefined -> [] (continuous); true -> all indices; array -> those indices
domain_schema.binary: an integer index whose bounds are lower===0 && upper===1 (classifyModel_ / buildVariableDomains_)
domain_schema.mixed: has continuous vars alongside integer/binary, OR both binary and plain-integer vars
domain_schema.metadata_only: buildVariableDomains_ produces the per-variable receipt; it does NOT solve

integrality_contract.note: applied only to declared integer indices; continuous vars are not integrality-checked

binary_contract.bounds: binary requires bounds {lower:0, upper:1}; supplied via model.bounds and folded by applyBounds_ (E3)
binary_contract.value_0_or_1: accepted; a fractional binary value is branched like any integer
binary_contract.classification: all-binary integer vars -> 'binary'; binary + plain integer -> 'mixed'; binary + continuous -> 'mixed'

node_schema.representation: recursive explore(extra, depth): extra = accumulated branch constraints, depth = tree depth
node_schema.root_relaxation: solveLinearProgram_ on model.constraints (no extra) at depth 0
node_schema.order: CEIL branch first ({coefficients:unit, relation:'>=', rhs:Math.ceil(value)}), then FLOOR ({relation:'<=', rhs:Math.floor(value)})
node_schema.incumbent_update: only if the snapped exact-integer objective strictly improves (maximise: > best+EPSILON; minimise: < best-EPSILON)
node_schema.snap: snapped = values.map(v=>Math.round(v*1e9)/1e9); then Math.round on integer indices; re-checked with feasibleAt_
pruning: bound: if incumbent exists and relaxed cannot beat it (+/-1e-9), return
infeasible: proven dead end, return (search stays exhaustive)
non-optimal non-infeasible (unbounded/numerical/iteration): mark search not exhaustive, record stopReason

limits.at_incumbent: limit reached WITH incumbent -> status 'feasible', optimalityProven false, stopReason set
limits.no_incumbent: limit reached WITHOUT incumbent -> status 'unknown', stopReason set (or 'iteration_limit')
limits.determinism_note: time_limit is tested with a Date.now() STUB (no real 20s wait); the stub returns a base time then a value past the deadline, hitting the exact deadline branch

fields: nodes (duplicate of nodesExplored on the success path)
result_schema.optimal: exhausted search with an incumbent -> optimal, optimalityProven true, stopReason null
result_schema.feasible: incumbent found but search stopped by a limit -> feasible, optimalityProven false
result_schema.infeasible: exhausted search, no incumbent -> infeasible, optimalityProven false
result_schema.unknown: non-exhausted search, no incumbent -> unknown, stopReason (time/node/iteration)
result_schema.note: these are INTERNAL contracts; the public status/stopReason/optimalityProven semantics remain E5 and are not redefined here

integer_cases.desc: integer 2 var max 3x+2y st x+y<=4 (already integral)
integer fractional relaxation max x+y st 2x+2y<=5
minimize integer min x st x>=1.5 (int)

mixed_cases.desc: mixed x continuous + y integer, max x+10y st x+y<=3.5

limit_cases.desc: time_limit without incumbent (Date stub jumps past deadline on 2nd call)
time_limit WITH incumbent (Date stub jumps after ~12 calls)
normal model does not hit any limit

continuous_bypass.contract: a fully-continuous model (integerIndices_ empty) is dispatched to solveLinearProgram_ and NEVER enters solveIntegerProgram_

No legacy suite was migrated or split (migrated 0, split 0): each reaches solveModel_ end-to-end and/or final-status assertions (E5). The new canonical E4 suites constitute the primary E4 coverage.

parity.rule: inputs that do not trigger the approved divergences must be exactly equal; a third divergence must fail; the mirror is never modified to force parity; nodesExplored/stopReason/optimalityProven/values order/constraints order/errors are never dropped
parity.note: isWhole_/solveIntegerProgram_/integerIndices_ are NOT exported by the mirror; their parity is covered observably through optimise_'s branch-and-bound results. classifyModel_ is the direct-parity case.
